questions.stemHtml: A 35-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 5-day history of a spreading rash. She reports that it began as a small red spot on her thigh that has expanded progressively and now measures approximately 15 cm in diameter. The lesion is not painful but feels warm to the touch. She recalls hiking in a heavily wooded area in the North-eastern United States two weeks prior. On examination, you observe a target like lesions as shown in the image below.
